title: Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts — Maintenance Records on Lubricated-Component Claims
content:
**The requirement.** A Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts claim for a failure of an internally lubricated component (engine, transmission or drive axle) requires proof of maintenance. The proof must show that manufacturer-scheduled oil and fluid services were done during the coverage level's maintenance look-back months before the failure.

**What counts as proof.**
- Repair orders recorded at any group store.
- Prepaid maintenance plan visits recorded at any group store.
- Receipts from other shops that the holder supplies.

The holder may not be required to use the selling store.

**When a claim is denied.** A lubricated-component claim is denied with the reason lack of maintenance only where both of the following hold:
- no qualifying service falls in the look-back window;
- the failure is of a kind caused by lack of lubrication.

**Components outside the requirement.** Failures of components that are not lubricated never need maintenance proof. These are the cooling, fuel system, electrical, air conditioning, steering, suspension, brakes, high-tech electronics and seals-and-gaskets groups.

| Claim | Qualifying service in the look-back window | Failure caused by lack of lubrication | Outcome under this rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transmission | shown (any group store, plan visit or outside receipt) | — | the maintenance requirement is met |
| Engine | none shown | yes | denied, lack of maintenance |
| Engine | none shown | no | this rule gives no denial |
| Air conditioning | — | — | no maintenance proof needed |
